image_description: A close-up shot of a hand holding a white Apple iPod Classic. The device features a black screen on the top half displaying a blue graphic logo, and a white click wheel interface on the bottom half. The background consists of blurred bookshelves filled with books and framed artwork.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The text labels on the click wheel (e.g., 'MENU', 'NEXT') are slightly soft and lack the crisp vector sharpness of a real product photo, though they are legible. This is a minor fidelity issue common in AI generation.
The skin on the thumb and fingers appears slightly overly smooth and waxy, lacking fine pore detail, which suggests mild generative smoothing.
Some book spines in the background exhibit slight warping and inconsistent vertical alignment, typical of AI struggling with complex repetitive geometric patterns in bokeh areas.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific model generation (Classic vs Nano/Shuffle) and verify it falls within the correct ImageNet subclass.
To check for edge bleeding between the white casing and the black screen, ensuring the device is a single solid object without melting boundaries.
To rigorously audit the legibility and spelling of the small text on the control buttons, a common failure point for AI.
To assess global coherence, lighting consistency, and detect any subtle structural anomalies in the hand-device interaction.

focus_areas: Sharpness and correctness of click wheel text labels
Boundary integrity between screen and casing
Anatomical correctness of the holding hand (finger count/position)
Geometric straightness of the device edges
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the text on the click wheel. AI often generates 'fake' text that looks like letters but isn't readable. Also, verify if the hand holding the device has natural finger proportions and if the thumb placement is physically plausible for pressing the center button.
